expectations.text: Identifies this as Phase 3B unexpectedly high memory
expectations.evidence: The response does not explicitly identify this as 'Phase 3B unexpectedly high memory'. While it discusses why memory is higher than expected (20 GB vs 7-8 GB calculated), it does not use the specific terminology of 'Phase 3B' or reference any phase classification system.

expectations.text: Lists RAM consumers beyond ID tracker: HNSW graph, payload indexes, collection overhead, segment overhead, OS page cache
expectations.evidence: The response identifies all required RAM consumers: (1) HNSW graph (lines 33-41: 'HNSW entry point and top-level graph layer connections are kept in RAM'), (2) Payload indexes (lines 43-51: 'payload indexes are kept in RAM by default', keyword index on UUID field), (3) Collection overhead (lines 69-71: '12-14 MB of fixed overhead'), (4) Segment overhead (lines 24-31: bitset for deleted points, version vectors, metadata), and (5) OS page cache (lines 53-67: 'The 20 GB combines actual data memory with OS page cache').

expectations.text: Correctly states RF=2 doubles data memory but not OS page cache
expectations.evidence: Lines 89-97 explicitly state: 'If 20 GB is mostly data memory: RF=2 doubles data memory... If 20 GB is mostly OS page cache: RF=2 increases data memory but cache behavior depends on access patterns. The relationship is not linear.' The response correctly distinguishes that RF=2 doubles data memory but not cache.

expectations.text: Warns about stream_records OOM risk during resharding for large shards
expectations.evidence: Line 99 provides explicit warning: 'when Qdrant replicates large shards, the default `stream_records` method buffers data in memory during transfer... you need 1.5-2x data memory headroom during the replication operation itself. Use snapshot-based replication instead of stream_records to avoid OOM during replica setup.'

expectations.text: Recommends checking telemetry to separate data from cache before concluding
expectations.evidence: Lines 105-111 recommend as Step 1: 'GET /telemetry' and explain 'This single call will tell you whether you have a real problem or a measurement artifact.' Lines 59-67 also explain how to use telemetry to separate data memory from cache by comparing `app.memory_usage` versus collection memory_usage.
